record.paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
record.context_brief: Topology of the admissible representation space
record.original_question: Fix a closed hyperbolic surface S of genus at least 2. Let Adm(S) be the space of admissible pairs (j,ρ) of representations π_1(S) → PSL_2(R) with j Fuchsian and such that the induced action on AdS^3 is properly discontinuous and cocompact. How many connected components does Adm(S) have, and what is its topology?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2. How many connected components does the space Adm(S) have? What is its topology?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $\Gamma = \pi_1(S)$. Identify three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ with the Lie group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ endowed with (a suitable rescaling of) its Killing form, so that its identity component of isometries is $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ acting by left and right multiplication. A pair of representations $(j, \rho) : \Gamma \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is called admissible if $j$ is Fuchsian (i.e., faithful and discrete with cocompact image) and the diagonal action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ via $\gamma \cdot x = j(\gamma)\, x\, \rho(\gamma)^{-1}$ is properly discontinuous and cocompact (equivalently, by Kulkarni–Raymond, $j$ strictly dominates $\rho$ in translation length). Let
$$\mathrm{Adm}(S) \;=\; \{(j,\rho) : j \text{ Fuchsian},\ (j,\rho) \text{ admissible}\} \subset \mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}))^2,$$
endowed with the subspace topology.

Determine the number of connected components of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ and describe its topology (e.g., its homotopy type).
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed. Salein, Kassel, Guéritaud–Kassel and others showed admissibility is equivalent to strict domination of $\rho$ by $j$ in translation length, and that $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ contains representations in many components of the relative representation variety. Deroin–Tholozan (2014) and Tholozan ("Dominating surface group representations and deforming closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds", Geom. Topol. 21 (2017), 193–246) proved that any non-Fuchsian representation $\rho$ into $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is strictly dominated by some Fuchsian $j$, and used this to describe the deformation space of closed AdS 3-manifolds; in particular each non-extremal component of $\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma,\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}))$ contributes to $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$, yielding the components and a description of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ as fibering over Teichmüller space. The fine topology (e.g. complete homotopy type) of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ is essentially understood through these works, though the question as originally posed is generally regarded as resolved by Tholozan's results.

status_evidence.title: Dominating surface group representations and deforming closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds (Tholozan)
status_evidence.snippet: Describes the deformation space of closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds via dominating Fuchsian representations, identifying the topology and connected components of the admissible space.
status_evidence.claim: The connected components and topology of Adm(S) are described via a fibration over Teichmüller space, resolving the question in essential form.

status_evidence.title: Dominating surface group representations by Fuchsian ones (Deroin–Tholozan)
status_evidence.snippet: Any representation of a closed surface group into PSL(2,R) of non-extremal Euler class is strictly dominated by a Fuchsian representation.
status_evidence.claim: Implies every non-extremal component of Hom(Γ, PSL_2(R)) contributes a component to Adm(S).

status_evidence.title: Deformations of Fuchsian AdS representations are quasi-Fuchsian (Barbot)
status_evidence.snippet: Quasi-Fuchsian AdS representations form a union of connected components of the representation variety.
status_evidence.claim: Provides component-level openness/closedness facts used in describing Adm(S).
